findings.title: Leave and rejoin by request in one assignment resets the player's spend count
findings.where: backend vtt/assignment.py release_from_campaign (end_assignment_for zeroes resources_spent_assignment) with vtt/routers/campaigns.py release_member; seam with #41 (backend/engine.py approve_investigator)
findings.steps: Sealed campaign R, spending open. Ros has used both spends this assignment (resources_spent_assignment=2). Ros leaves (POST /campaign/release, or Leave on the desk). The backend restarts (optional). Ros asks to join R again and the Lightkeeper approves.
findings.expected: The decisions cap circle spends at two per player per assignment, and #41 makes a replacement keep its predecessor's count. A member coming back in the same assignment would keep the count.
findings.actual: Ros is active again with resources_spent_assignment=0 and can spend two more this assignment. Pools are not refilled, so only the per-player cap is bypassed, and it needs the Lightkeeper's approval.

findings.steps: Open Edit sheet, change pronouns. The server sees the investigator as dead (SQL is_dead=true while the dialog is open). Press Save.
findings.expected: One alert, in the reopened dialog that holds the draft.
findings.actual: Two role=alert elements say 'Rux Ollinor is dead: the sheet is a record.', one in the dialog and one under the sheet behind it, so a screen reader announces it twice. The draft itself is kept correctly.

method: Folder /home/user/pt4/verify/lifecycle. lib.js is a copy of v8405_lib.js with ports and DB picked by env T=main|control (main api 8120/site 4120/db pt4_main_8120, control 8121/4121/pt4_control_8121); state in state_<T>.json, shots in out_<T>/. setup.js builds both tables through the API (6 accounts lk,pa..pe; campaign S sealed with 4 members and relationships, campaign U unsealed with 3), sealed in SQL. Per item scripts: s49_lk.js (release after seal), s49_leave.js (desk leave phone + second tab), s49_hub.js (hub leave, pre-seal release and leave), s49_edge.js (crafted releases, leave/rejoin with restart_api.sh), s50.js (Train dice, End Assignment, restart, wording, roll), s38.js and s38ui.js (dead refusals REST+WS, dead paper, #22 after retiring D), s39.js (rejoin from second device, #41), s42.js (fresh campaigns P1/P2 retired while the hub is open, double Play; #47 Registry), s64.js, s69.js and s64_scar.js (Edit sheet, gear diff using a Lightkeeper End Assignment while the gear dialog is open, refused save by setting is_dead in SQL while the editor is open, crafted fourth scar), s66.js (69.7 crafted update_circle on an unsealed circle, #66 stamp chooser, Undo, reload), probe.js (dump visible buttons). Avoid: opening a Node wsOpen socket on a character whose desk is open in the browser; it takes the desk ('open in another tab') and the page's later saves are lost; use the Lightkeeper's socket for table-side changes instead. Registry Leave buttons are named '<name> leaves <campaign>' and Play buttons '<name><campaign>Play'. Retiring S/U consumes them, so later checks need fresh campaigns. Servers were stopped and both databases dropped at the end. About 85 tool calls.
praise: Release and leave reach every desk live, including a second tab of the leaving player, and a double press sends one request.
The dead-record refusals are uniform: REST and WebSocket, proposal and counter, both directions, with the same plain sentence.
The gear dialog applies only its own diff, so an End Assignment while it is open is not undone.
Edit sheet writes one readable log line naming every change, from and to, and the roster dot clears when the Lightkeeper opens the sheet.
Train dice survive End Assignment and a server restart, and every surface uses the same 'kept until a roll uses it' wording.
